behavioral_notes.element: repair.order state machine: action_validate -> _action_repair_confirm / action_repair_start / action_repair_end -> action_repair_done / action_repair_cancel
behavioral_notes.observation: State flows draft -> confirmed -> under_repair -> done (or -> cancel). action_validate checks on-hand qty of the product-to-repair at product_location_src_id (owner first, then no-owner) and either calls _action_repair_confirm or raises the stock.warn.insufficient.qty.repair wizard. _action_repair_confirm (draft->confirmed) runs move_ids._adjust_procure_method(picking_type_code='repair_operation'), _action_confirm(), then _trigger_scheduler() to procure parts. action_repair_start (confirmed->under_repair) confirms first if still draft. action_repair_end requires state=='under_repair' then delegates to action_repair_done. action_repair_cancel cancels all part moves and zeroes the bound sale.order.line qty. None of this transition logic is visible in metadata.

behavioral_notes.element: repair.order.action_repair_done -> stock.move creation (consume parts + produce repaired product)
behavioral_notes.observation: On completion it cancels zero-qty part moves, marks remaining part moves picked=True, and CREATES a new stock.move (stored as move_id) for the product-to-repair from product_location_src_id to product_location_dest_id, whose move.line consume_line_ids link the consumed parts' move lines for traceability. It then calls (move_ids + product_move)._action_done(cancel_backorder=True), committing all moves to stock.quant, and sets state='done'. The repaired good is thus 'produced' as a stock.move into a production-type location while 'add' parts are consumed from stock.

Each part move carries repair_line_type. Locations are computed from the repair order per type: 'add' = location_id -> location_dest_id (into the production/repair location; _is_consuming() returns True so it draws down stock); 'remove' = location_dest_id -> parts_location_id (inventory-loss/scrap); 'recycle' = location_dest_id -> recycle_location_id. Repair moves bypass normal reservation and split (_should_be_assigned and _split return early) and take repair_id.picking_type_id rather than living on a stock.picking. This is how a repair both consumes added parts and disposes of removed/recycled parts as distinct inventory flows.

Confirming a sale.order calls order_line._create_repair_order(): for each line whose product_template service_tracking == 'repair' (qty > 0, not already bound) it creates a confirmed repair.order linked via sale_order_id/sale_order_line_id with picking_type from warehouse.repair_type_id. Conversely 'add' part moves on the RO auto-create sale.order.line records (_create_repair_sale_order_line) so added parts are billed; under_warranty=True forces price_unit/technical_price_unit to 0. On action_repair_done qty_delivered is set from the repaired/part moves (_prepare_qty_delivered), feeding the standard sale invoicing flow. The link is bidirectional and not derivable from metadata.

A repair can originate from a return transfer: stock.picking.action_repair_return opens a repair.order form pre-seeded with default_repair_picking_id and partner, and picking_id is domain-restricted to pickings with return_id != False. _compute_partner_id, _compute_product_qty and compute_lot_id derive the customer, quantity and lot/serial from that return picking's move lines, wiring the reverse-logistics chain (delivery -> customer return -> repair) without any explicit FK that metadata could surface.

classification.rationale: Repair is a value-chain (transform/flow) configuration: a physical good moves through an operation that consumes inputs (spare parts drawn from stock as 'add' moves, _is_consuming=True) and produces an output (the serviced product re-created as a stock.move into a production location and committed to stock.quant via _action_done). The append-only stock-move ledger plus bill-of-parts consumption is textbook chain logic - the same logistics machinery as stock/mrp, applied after the original sale. It is classed activity_class='support' rather than primary because, like maintenance, it is an after-sales / aftermarket service that restores already-delivered products rather than being the firm's primary make-and-ship flow; it depends on sale_stock+sale_management and only runs when a return or a service line triggers it. APQC 4.0 'Deliver Physical Products' is the closest umbrella: repair is reverse logistics / after-sales operations - it operates inbound from a customer return (4.4.x outbound transportation run in reverse), manages parts inventory (4.3.2.1 manage raw material inventory, via stock.quant moves and warehouse.repair_mto_pull_id replenishment) and re-delivers the serviced good. No single 4.x leaf names 'repair', so 4.0 is taken with the after-sales/reverse-logistics qualification; a 7.x 'customer service / after-sales support' reading is plausible, but the dominant evidence (stock.move consumption/production, repair picking types, warehouse routing) is physical fulfilment, hence 4.0.

Whether removed/recycled parts (remove->inventory-loss, recycle->recycle location) post any valuation entry (boundary with stock_account).
